title: Speedrun SDK MiniHack Playbook (sketch)
content:
Purpose:

Quick, runnable playbook for a 30–90 minute internal mini-hack using the Redwood SDKs. Make it low friction so engineers can validate a feature, gather telemetry, and produce a tiny demo. This doc is a sketch for the pilot that we can iterate on during the next DevEx sync.

Audience:
- New joiners who need a fast path to a working sample
- Field engineers preparing a 15–minute demo
- Developer advocates running an internal workshop

Success criteria (pilot):
- 80% of participants finish a working mini-app within 60 minutes
- SDK usage captures token counts + latency + sampling params in prod-like telemetry
- At least one feedback PR to improve docs or snippets

Run formats (pick one):
- Speedrun (15–30 mins): tiny curl/JS example, streaming demo, single-file repo
- MiniHack (45–90 mins): small multi-file sample app + test prompts + telemetry assertions
- Guided lab (90+ mins): instructor-led with checkpoints and failure-mode exercises

Core components to include in kit:
1) 5-min Quickstart script (copy-paste)
2) 3 runnable snippets (curl, JS, Python) that cover: simple completion, chat call, embedding+search
3) Telemetry checklist (what events to emit and why)
4) One-page failure modes (quota, rate-limit, large output)
5) Minimal CI smoke test (asserts response schema + basic latency)
6) Post-mortem template for what to capture after the hack

5-minute Quickstart (copyable):
- Create API key: REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxxxx
- Run sample (node):

// sample app: speedrun.js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-small:1', prompt: 'Write a 2-line haiku about coffee.', max_tokens: 40 })
  });
  console.log(await res.text());
})();

- Or curl: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small:1","prompt":"Hello world","max_tokens":20}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Telemetry checklist (quick):
- events/hack.start (attrs: template, runner_id)
- events/request.sent (attrs: model, seq_len, prompt_tokens, max_tokens, batching_on)
- events/response.received (attrs: latency_ms, tokens_generated, streaming?)
- events/hack.complete (attrs: success:boolean, demo_url?)
- Log sample payloads for at least 3 runs (redact user data)

Telemetry notes:
- Use the SDK’s telemetry helper wrapper so we can correlate token counts to latency easily. Add a single flag --telemetry-debug to surface sample payloads to console.

MiniHack flow (45–90 mins):
- 0–10m: setup (env, install, API key)
- 10–25m: run 3 core snippets (completion, chat, embeddings search)
- 25–45m: extend one snippet (add context, chain calls, KV cache emulation)
- 45–60m: add telemetry asserts + run CI smoke test locally
- 60–90m: demo + collect feedback in PR template

Sample task idea (pick one):
- Tiny assistant: read a short product doc (3 paragraphs), answer 3 questions, return sources + confidence score
- Smart subject-line generator: given email body, produce 5 subject-line variants and rank them by length & subjectivity
- Fast semantic search: index 5 short docs using embeddings, then run 5 queries and show results with similarity scores

Minimal CI smoke (bash):
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e
RESP=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-small:1","prompt":"Ping","max_tokens":5}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate)
if [[ $RESP == *"Ping"* ]]; then echo "smoke ok"; else echo "smoke fail"; exit 1; fi

Failure modes (common & suggested mitigations):
- 429 rate-limit during hack: set smaller batch, exponential backoff demo snippet, or switch to smaller model
- Long-tail latency: use streaming snippet to show progressive output; explain prefix caching
- Unexpected output format: add strict output schema + example tests in snippet

Doc ergonomics (how the kit should read):
- Single README that surfaces 3 fastest paths (15m, 45m, 90m)
- Each snippet lives in /examples/<lang>/<task>/README.md (one-liner + expected output)
- One folder /telemetry with helpers and a sample dashboard json (simple CSV acceptable)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we bake a tiny web UI (static) or keep everything CLI-first? (Pros: demos look nicer; Cons: more moving parts)
- Which models do we default to for the Speedrun? (redwood-small:1 vs community open models)
- Decide whether to auto-create demo credentials scoped to a single IP during workshops

Post-mortem PR template (fill after each run):
- date:
- runner:
- format (speedrun/minihack/guided):
- ran to completion? yes/no:
- issues encountered (brief):
- telemetry exported? yes/no + link:
- doc changes suggested (line refs):

Success metrics to record for pilot:
- % finish within target time (15/45/90)
- # of PRs improving snippets/docs
- median latency observed across runs
- tokens per successful demo

Next steps (owner + ETA):
- Maya: draft canonical 15m speedrun README (ETA: 2024-11-12)
- Ethan: add telemetry wrapper and example CSV exporter (ETA: 2024-11-19)
- Priya: produce the Python + JS snippet set and test matrix (ETA: 2024-11-22)

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Keep each example hermetic: avoid external network calls other than Redwood API
- Encourage participants to open a tiny PR that documents one pain point — that drives product improvements
- Consider a reproducible devcontainer for guided labs later

Links & references:
- Quick reference for SDK auth: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVEX/SDK+AUTH
- Mini-hack retrospective template: JIRA:DX-412
- Example repo: GH:repo/sdk-examples/tree/minihack

End of sketch — keep this lightweight. We want something that can be copied into a README in <30 minutes and then improved based on real run feedback.
